content: There are two common modeling methods for basic NLP tasks, including n-gram model and bag-of-words model. The n-gram model is widely used in natural language processing while the bag-of-words model is a simplified representation used in natural language processing and information retrieval BIBREF17 , BIBREF18 . According to the bag-of-words model, the representative vector of sentences in the document does not preserve the order of the words in the original sentences. It represents the word using term frequency collected from the document rather than the order of words or the structure of sentences in the document. The bag-of-words model is commonly used in methods of document classification, where the frequency of occurrence of each word is used as an attribute feature for training a classifier. In contrast, an n-gram is a contiguous sequence of n items from a given sequence of text. An n-gram model is a type of probabilistic language model for predicting the next item in a given sequence in form of a Markov model. To address word segmentation issue, the n-gram model is usually used for approaches because it considers the order of tokens in the original sentences. The sequence is also kept the original order as input and output sentences.
